  [DOC: airlines_fy2022_fy2024.txt]

  • 2023→2024: (61,643 − 58,048) / 58,048 ≈ **6.2%**

  • 2023→2024: (57,063 − 53,717) / 53,717 ≈ **6.2%**

  • 2022→2023: (26,091 − 23,814) / 23,814 ≈ **9.6%**  
  • 2023→2024: (27,483 − 26,091) / 26,091 ≈ **5.3%**

  • 2022→2023: (52,788 − 48,971) / 48,971 ≈ **7.8%**  
  • 2023→2024: (54,211 − 52,788) / 52,788 ≈ **2.7%**

- **Alaska** (note: 2024 includes Hawaiian)  
  • 2022→2023: (10,426 − 9,646) / 9,646 ≈ **8.1%**  
  • 2023→2024: (11,735 − 10,426) / 10,426 ≈ **12.6%**

Because Hawaiian contributed **$869M** of Alaska’s 2024 revenue, a material portion of that ~12.6% growth is acquisition-driven rather than organic. [DOC: alaska_10k_note_acquisition.txt]

**Step 3 – “Revenue growth momentum” through FY 2024**

A simple way to interpret “momentum” is whether growth is **accelerating or decelerating** from 2022→2023 to 2023→2024:

- Delta, United, Southwest, and American all show **slower** growth in 2023→2024 than in 2022→2023 (growth deceleration).
- Alaska is the only one with **higher** reported growth in 2023→2024 (≈12.6%) than in 2022→2023 (≈8.1%), i.e., **accelerating** reported revenue growth. But this acceleration is significantly driven by the addition of Hawaiian’s revenue starting September 18, 2024, which makes Alaska’s growth **not strictly comparable** to its own prior years or to peers who did not add such a large acquired revenue base. [DOC: alaska_10k_note_acquisition.txt]

If you define “strongest revenue growth momentum” purely by the **reported** acceleration in year-on-year revenue growth, Alaska ranks highest, albeit for inorganic (M&A) reasons rather than underlying demand alone.

ANSWER: Alaska Air Group (with the important caveat that its FY 2024 revenue growth momentum is boosted by the Hawaiian Airlines acquisition and is not fully comparable to the other carriers’ organic trends).
